Leading excellence in inclusive practice for children and young people with physical and mental health needs, enabling every child to learn, achieve and thrive through access to the right support at the right time
"The teachers are incredible they have made me actually enjoy school for the first time in a long time, they made me feel understood and worked with me to embrace my interests and achieve my goals. i love the variety of lessons and how each lesson can be understood by a 12 year old and a 17 year old as they are adapted to all of us. the teachers are so passionate and make me really excited to learn new things and engage with the lessons."
Pupil Questionnaire, 2025
"The friendly teachers that are all amazing!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!"
Pupil Questionnaire, 2024
"The teachers have been amazing from day 1, they have made such a difference to our daughter’s education and well-being. Their smiles and manner mean they are secure adults for her and she is like a different child. She wants to learn. She wants to study. The painting lesson on the common was the educational highlight for the past 2 years."
"Thank you for supporting her and being there for her, you've been a lifeline to her."
"Thank you for your flexibility. Nothing has been too much. You just don't get provisions like these elsewhere."
"We can’t thank you enough for providing a lovely school environment for our son whilst he was on the ward. He absolutely loved going to your school and learning, and was so upset to miss his usual school routine whilst he was in hospital for such a long time. He was delighted that you had the fun, interest and maths games that he loved, gave him a break from his bed, lent him books and games and engaged him so kindly. From painting socks to a virtual museum visit, you helped him to keep a sense of who he was and what he liked. Thank you again from us and Edward."
"Most pupils have missed long periods of learning due to illness. They make remarkable progress during their short time in the school."
"We are so grateful and thankful for the brilliant staff at the St. George’s Hospital School. We have spent quite a lot of time there over the past 18 months, they have made learning such fun – memorable science experiments and story writing, the best time making posters and adverts and treats for the school cafe. The staff are cheerful, calm, gentle and above all fun. Thank you to the great team."
"The pupils who attend this school are undeniably proud and happy here….. "
Ofsted, October 2023
"Wow, where to begin. I wanted to write to you to demonstrate how much of a positive impact you have had on me……you have restored my faith in teachers everywhere...the CAMHS Campus School was definitely the highlight of Springfield for me as is the case for so many others."
"Pupils’ behaviour is exemplary both in class and throughout the school. They are polite, welcoming, and cooperative… "
Ofsted, October 2023
"Every day my son looks forward to going to school – to get away from his room, and all the poking and prodding from doctors is such a relief. He is treated like a school boy, rather than a patient, and I think this has as much healing properties as medicine! Due to his illness, my son has missed about a month of schooling, but hopefully will have caught up because of the hospital school."
"We are so grateful that there is a school/classroom to attend. J really needs something to focus on when he’s in hospital, he looks forward to getting out of his room and working/studying English, Maths and other interesting topics he can learn about. It has really made a difference to his mood during the hospital stays, having been admitted so many times throughout the past 7 months. Furthermore, it helps him keep on top of his schooling."
"When pupils join, staff promptly establish a connection with them, making an effort to understand each pupil’s personality, interests, talents and future aspirations….."
Ofsted, October 2023
"Parents and carers praise the teaching staff for their compassionate, nurturing approach. They recognise the school as being exceptional."
Ofsted, October 2023
"Leaders have designed a highly effective and ambitious curriculum. It reflects leaders determination that every pupil should benefit from a rich and engaging learning experience…."
Ofsted, October 2023
"I was blown away with your manner with A . I am thrilled with how the visit went, I have not seen ‘A’ that calm/engaged for a long time and it has made my year! "
Social worker, November 2023
"The difference in him is like day and night. Best place for him -( lots and lots of praise for Compass), these teachers always say positive things about him, seem to understand him, he's never spent so long at school,he doesn't seem depressed anymore, had he not come to you we think he would have not lived Can he stay here next year?"
Parent, October 2023
"J feels that the Camhs School at Springfield is the first place he has felt accepted and that the teachers understand him and his needs. This breaks my heart to hear him say this bearing in mind he is in y11 but highlights the need that there must be something similar to the way Camhs School work away from the hospital and I wonder if this can be considered."
Parent, October 2023
" Pupils are enthusiastic about learning because lessons are enjoyable and captivating…. "
Ofsted, October 2023
"Since the beginning of my admission every single staff in school has helped me feel more confident in a school environment and also helped me feel less stressed about going back into education outside of hospital. I love the CAMHS School and all the teachers there, I am so grateful for you all, you are all inspirations. I’m so lucky to have met you all. Thank you for everything. All my love and thanks"
"Since the beginning of my admission every single staff in school has helped me feel more confident in a school environment and also helped me feel less stressed about going back into education outside of hospital. I love the CAMHS School and all the teachers there, I am so grateful for you all, you are all inspirations. I’m so lucky to have met you all. Thank you for everything. All my love and thanks"
"I want to congratulate you for the amazing team you have. I couldn’t start to describe how incredible teachers, and most importantly individuals they are. I feel extremely blessed to have the opportunity to have their support in the worst moments of my son and my life: and that they were part of our lives. Thanks to your team N- can boast about the great results he has in his GCSEs being one of the best in his group of friends. This has helped his self-esteem immensely."
"To everyone at school, Thank you so much for supporting me throughout my admission and making it possible to keep up with all my A=Level work whilst being here! I am so grateful! Sorry I didn't manage to say a proper goodbye and I hope this card finds you well :). Thank you again! I’ll make sure I’ll never be back :) Love, M"
"It’s been a long time coming but I’m finally leaving and moving on. I want to thank you all so much for your help, I am ever so grateful! I wouldn’t be where I am today if I didn’t have school… not only that but I never thought I could do the things that I can do. You’ve all had so much hope in me and you’ve all been so patient and understanding. Being on a ward isn’t the best…I was honestly getting to a point where I was just going to give up on school because I didn’t see myself doing anything but that thought has changed, thanks to you all!!! You're all so kind and understanding, you have had such an impact on me, you’ve helped me so much and I can’t describe how grateful I am.!!!"
"“I am not sure if you remember me. I hope that it is okay that I got your email from your website. I just wanted to reiterate how grateful I am for all the support you gave me over my time at Wisteria. I am so thankful for all your encouragement to keep motivated with school work. You are such a wonderful school service and I am sure you have helped many others like you have helped me. I was writing in regards to the GCSE grades I managed to get predicted so far this school year. I couldn’t have done it without you. Grade 9 in maths, Thanks Sandra !!! An 8/9 in English language and literature Thanks Sally !!! And 9 in biology, chemistry and physics. Thank you Jess !!! 9 in geography, psychology, and Spanish. I am just so eternally grateful for the education you provided me and so thankful you never gave put on pushing us to reach our full potential. I will never forget the school.”"
“To Corner House teaching team at CAMHS School, You are more than welcome, it was the very least we could do. We literally can’t thank you all enough for everything you have done for M, as well as the support you have shown us. The help you’ve all given with regards to the next school and securing the transport has been amazing. I know M will miss you all but after having the opportunity to come to your school he has managed to build on his confidence and self-belief. I honestly feel like this has given him the foundation to thrive at The Deaf Academy. I have filled in the questionnaire. If there’s anything else you need from me please just let me know. I hope M has a good last week. Thank you so much once again. Julie."
"I wouldn't want to change anything about the service, they have been absolutely brilliant! I literally couldn't fault them at all and am extremely grateful for everything they have done for my child."

Mission statement
We believe in a holistic approach to learning; we ensure that all children have the best possible education during an unsettling period in their lives. We foster a sense of wonder and aim to bring a love of learning that they can take with them throughout life. We consider a student’s holistic development to be as valuable as their academic progress. We encourage ourselves and our young people to develop resilience, empathy and advocacy in order to work towards an equitable society for all.
HHTS joins together every facet of our students’ care with their personal learning journey. Through respectful and kind relationships, individualised learning and dynamic interventions we ensure our students have every opportunity to discover and realise their potential and aspirations.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Wandsworth Hospital & Home Tuition School
pageCache.text:
Leading excellence in inclusive practice for children and young people with physical and mental health needs, enabling every child to learn, achieve and thrive through access to the right support at the right time
HHTS has a long history of delivering exceptional education for students who are unable to attend their mainstream school due to a diagnosed medical condition. Our teaching approach, ethos and personalised curriculum offer ensures that pupils make accelerated academic progress in a safe, welcoming and supportive environment.
The service is comprised of 9 sectors operating over two sites, St George’s School at St Georges Hospital and CAMHS Campus School at Springfield University Hospital:
Springfield University Hospital – CAMHS Campus School
This school is adjacent to the CAMHS inpatients wards and offers a full academic timetable for inpatients.
St George’s Hospital School
This school is located on the fifth floor of St George’s Hospital adjacent to the paediatric wards. The team offer a full timetable in the schoolroom and academic tuition at the bedside for inpatients.
Wandsworth Community Statutory Duty
Home Tuition Primary and Secondary- Medical
The Home Tuition Service is for children and young people resident in Wandsworth, who are unable to attend school due to an underlying medical condition.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head’s Welcome | Wandsworth Hospital & Home Tuition School
pageCache.text:
Leading excellence in inclusive practice for children and young people with physical and mental health needs, enabling every child to learn, achieve and thrive through access to the right support at the right time
It is my pleasure to welcome you to the website of the Hospital and Home Tuition Service (HHTS) in Wandsworth.
WHHTS is comprised of St. Georges Hospital School, Springfield Hospital school at CAMHS Campus, Wandsworth Medical PRU (home tuition), and educational outreach services for children who are too unwell or struggling to attend school due to physical or mental ill health.
Our students have the opportunity to make accelerated progress through personalised learning programmes delivered by exceptional practitioners in small groups or in one-to-one tuition. Staff and students build positive nurturing relationships enabling students to grow in confidence, self-acceptance, and compassion for all. Our approach is underpinned by our UNICEF Right Respecting values based on the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and focused on developing every child’s uniqueness, wellbeing and potential.
We provide a full and varied curriculum that ensures high standards of academic challenge and achievement while offering breadth of opportunity. Our curriculums are enhanced by inspiring experiences from a wealth of cultural partners. This dual approach offers both depth and breadth; enabling our students to keep up with or exceed their peers academically, whilst developing new skills and interests and an understanding of the positive difference they can make to the world.
Across each provision, close links with medical professionals and members of the multidisciplinary teams, home school staff, CAMHS and other stakeholders enable students to thrive. I hope that this website will help you find out more about our unique and engaging service.
If you require more information or would like to visit, please contact info@hhts.wandsworth.sch.uk
Tara Bell

pageCache.text:
Leading excellence in inclusive practice for children and young people with physical and mental health needs, enabling every child to learn, achieve and thrive through access to the right support at the right time
The Wandsworth Hospital & Home Tuition Service is committed to providing appropriate, high quality education. We believe that all children and young people, including those identified as having a special educational need or a disability (SEND), have a common entitlement to a strong academic and social curriculum which is accessible to them. Our SEND Policy makes explicit our approach in this regard.
Furthermore, we believe that all children should be equally valued in education. We strive to eliminate prejudice and discrimination, and to develop an environment where all children and young people can flourish and feel safe. Our Equality and Disability Policy, in part, underscores this commitment.
The SEN LA Local Offer
The Local Offer has set out to transform the landscape of special educational needs and disability provision to ensure that all children with SEND can enjoy a high quality educational experience and work towards positive life outcomes and opportunities. It provides opportunities for families of children to collaboratively secure the support they require from providers within their locality. Young adults are also able to search for services that match their requirements through person-centred planning, and local commissioners of services, schools and other professionals can access a growing network of providers from all sectors across education, health and social care. This is the ‘Local Offer’.

pageCache.text:
Leading excellence in inclusive practice for children and young people with physical and mental health needs, enabling every child to learn, achieve and thrive through access to the right support at the right time
National Careers Week March 2025
This year, we are celebrating National Careers week by inviting in a range of speakers for our students to meet and explore different career pathways. Thank you to all the visitors who have volunteered to come in.
More information about National Careers week can be found here: https://nationalcareersweek.com/
Careers at HHTS
We offer personalised support to our pupils in their choices for the next stage of education, employment, and self-employment or training. We ensure that all of our long-term pupils receive careers guidance.
As well as a careers focus to each of the subjects taught, we also host a dedicated Careers Week in March.
We are already implementing the Gatsby Benchmarks – a framework of 8 guidelines that define the best careers provision in schools and colleges.
As well as working alongside the multi-disciplinary teams on the wards to help support next steps in education/employment for our pupils, we work closely with schools and colleges to ensure the best pathway forwards.
Our Careers Lead is Lynda Robinson and she can be contacted at admin@hhts.wandsworth.sch.uk
Methods used to assess impact
The impact of the Careers programme at Wandsworth HHTS is measured and assessed through pupil and student voice and by analysing destinations of leavers. Parents and carers have an important role to play in supporting their child in relation to their career journey and therefore we welcome feedback on the careers programme through the parent questionnaire on our website. In addition, we seek feedback from the staff team, governors and employers and a termly evaluation using Compass+ is conducted.
